headline: Rate Fears and Hormuz Tensions Frame a Cautious Setup
body_html:
Wall Street gets Wednesday's session underway nursing a loss from Tuesday, when a hot inflation reading and pointed Fed commentary stoked fresh worries about interest rates. Of the 667 stocks we track, 239 rose while 423 fell, a lopsided tilt toward decliners that sets the tone heading into the pre-market hours.

Rate-sensitive groups took the heaviest damage. Homebuilders dropped 3.47 percent, financials slid 2.5 percent and materials lost 1.54 percent. Semiconductors, healthcare, industrials and software each gave up between 0.61 and 0.75 percent. Energy was the only sector to finish higher, gaining 0.33 percent as crude rebounded after attacks on Hormuz shipping undercut hopes for an Iran truce.

At the open, watch three things. First, whether Fed officials' willingness to entertain a half-point rate hike keeps pressure on homebuilders and financials. Second, whether oil holds its rebound while tankers in the Middle East continue to burn. Third, whether Tuesday's outsized single-stock moves, from AAON's 19.31 percent surge to the 16.61 percent drop at Hims & Hers Health, see follow-through. Early pre-market prints are thin and can mislead, so patience is warranted.

briefs.headline: Fed Officials Leave Room for a Bigger Hike
briefs.body: Several Fed officials signaled they would consider a half-percentage-point increase in rates if inflation keeps worsening. Coming after a hot inflation reading, the remarks pushed rate worries to the front of investors' minds and weighed on stocks Tuesday. Traders will parse any further central-bank commentary today.

briefs.headline: Oil Rebounds as Shipping Attacks Cloud Truce Hopes
briefs.body: Crude bounced back Tuesday after strikes on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz dampened expectations of an Iran truce. Tankers in the region were still burning despite talk of de-escalation. Energy was the only sector in the green, up 0.33 percent, and the open will show whether the bid lasts.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders and Financials Lead the Retreat
briefs.body: Homebuilders fell 3.47 percent and financials dropped 2.5 percent, the two weakest sectors in our universe on Tuesday. Both groups are sensitive to the path of interest rates, and the prospect of a larger Fed hike gave sellers a clear reason to act. Materials also slipped 1.54 percent.

briefs.headline: AAON Jumps Nearly 20 Percent; Acadia and Zeta Also Climb
briefs.body: Among the session's biggest winners, AAON in HVAC surged 19.31 percent, Acadia Pharmaceuticals rose 10.79 percent and marketing-software firm Zeta Global gained 8.17 percent. Liquidia added 7.37 percent. Such strong moves against a weak tape deserve a look at the open for signs of continuation or fading.

briefs.headline: Hims & Hers, Legend Biotech, Novanta and Qualys Slump
briefs.body: Hims & Hers Health fell 16.61 percent and Legend Biotech lost 15.97 percent. Novanta dropped 15.26 percent and cybersecurity firm Qualys gave back 13.51 percent. Furniture maker Ethan Allen also fell 11.36 percent. Watch whether these stocks stabilize or keep sliding in early trade.

briefs.headline: Energy Supply Jitters Reach Europe and Iran's Gas Fields
briefs.body: Poland's Orlen ended a long-term liquefied natural gas contract with QatarEnergy, citing failures to deliver cargoes. Separately, a fire at a South Pars gas platform in Iran was reported contained. Together, the items underline how fragile energy supply looks while Gulf tensions persist.
